text:
Predicates:
Employees(x) ::: x is an employee.
Schedules(x, y) ::: x schedules a meeting with y.
Customer(y) ::: y is a customer.
InCompanyToday(x) ::: x appears in the company today.
Lunch(x, y) ::: x has lunch at y.
Home(y) ::: y is at home.
Remote(x) ::: x is working remotely.
InOtherCountry(x) ::: x is in another country.
Manager(x) ::: x is a manager.
James ::: James is a specific individual.

Premises:
∀x (Employees(x) ∧ Schedules(x, y) ∧ Customer(y) → InCompanyToday(x)) ::: All employees who schedule a meeting with their customers will appear in the company today.
∀x (Lunch(x, y) ∧ InCompany(y)) → Schedules(x, y) ::: Everyone who has lunch in the company schedules meetings with their customers.
∀x (Lunch(x, y)) (Lunch(x, y) ∧ (y = Home) ∨ InCompany(y)) ::: Employees will either have lunch in the company or at home.
∀x (Lunch(x, Home)) → Remote(x) ::: If an employee has lunch at home, then he/she is working remotely from home.
∀x (InOtherCountry(x)) → Remote(x) ::: All employees in other countries work remotely from home.
¬∃x (Manager(x) ∧ Remote(x)) ::: No managers work remotely from home.
James ::: James is either a manager and appears in the company today or neither a manager nor appears in the company today.

Conclusion:
InCompanyToday(James) ∧ Lunch(James, y) ::: James has lunch in the company.
